## MindMosaic Parent Journey — Phase P3 (Child Management and Profiles)

Implements the approved Claude Design Artboards b11–b14 (Children, Children — tablet, Children — mobile, Children states, A child’s profile).

---

### 1. Delivery & Architecture
- **Dedicated Worktree:** \C:\tmp\wt-pj-p3\ on branch \ eat/parent-child-profiles\.
- **Predecessor:** Built upon verified Phase P2 foundation (\ eat/parent-family-overview\ PR #107).
- **Zero Schema Mutations:** Preserves Supabase RLS and existing service-role boundary (\provisionChild\, \/api/parent/children/[childId]\).

---

### 2. Implemented Features & Screens
1. **Children List (\/parent/children\)**:
   - **Paid Places Banner (Decision P5)**: Clearly displays places used vs total plan seats (\2 of 3 used on your Family plan\, \1 place free\, link to \/parent/account\). Separates seats from student records.
   - **Your Children Card**: Interactive list of linked children with colored initial avatars, display names, year levels, login codes, and status badges (\Can sign in\ vs \Paused\).
   - **Direct Navigation**: \Manage\ (links to \/parent/children/[id]\) and \Progress\ (links to \/parent/children/[id]/curriculum\).
   - **How Your Children Sign In**: Educational guidance on non-changing login codes and 6-digit PINs, with shared computer advice.
   - **Print Sign-in Card**: Action modal generating clean printable cards formatted for student handoff.
   - **Archived Profiles (Decision P6)**: Reversible deactivation with instant \Restore\ capability.
2. **Child Profile View (\/parent/children/[childId]\)**:
   - **Breadcrumb & Header**: Contextual breadcrumb \Children / [Child Name]\ with status and finished paper counts.
   - **Sibling Switcher Tabs**: Effortlessly navigate between children without leaving profile views.
   - **Details Card**: Editable first name, year level selection, and 4-palette avatar color picker.
   - **Student Access Card**: Non-changing login code, PIN status (\Set · 6 digits\), last signed in timestamp, and direct action triggers.
   - **Three-State PIN Reset Dialog (Decision P7)**:
     - 1. *Confirm*: Explains instant sign-out while retaining work.
     - 2. *Done (Shown Once)*: Prominently renders the fresh 6-digit PIN in high-contrast boxes with strict reminder.
     - 3. *Failed*: Clear assurance that the old PIN remains active.
   - **Pausing & Lifecycle (Decision P6)**: Explains reversible pause and shared guardian access.
   - **Deletion Proposal Card (Decision P11 / ADR-012)**: Honest 30-day out-of-band erasure request.

---

### 3. Verification & Quality Gates
- **TypeScript:** \
pm run typecheck\ -> **PASS** (0 errors).
- **Unit & Component Tests:** 21 component tests passed (\children-manager.test.tsx\, \child-profile-view.test.tsx\, \pin-reset-dialog.test.tsx\). Total Parent suite: 132 tests passed.
- **Next.js Webpack Production Build:** Compiled all 70 routes including dynamic \/parent/children/[childId]\ -> **PASS** (0 errors).
- **Playwright Responsive Verification:** 11 screenshots captured across Desktop (1440px), Tablet (834px), and Mobile (390px) in \docs/audits/screenshots/p3/\.

Revise the Phase 2 proposal in response to independent adversarial review.
Documentation only: no code, schema, gate or question content changes.

Evidence correction. The candidate-impact analysis misstated the answer key
for nine of twelve candidates and misdescribed nr-023 and vr-016. It is
withdrawn and replaced by source-evidence-reconciliation.{md,json}, generated
mechanically by reconcile.py from PR #73 at dcb60a80 plus the Phase 1
preflight. The reconciliation reports inconsistencies rather than repairing
them, and found none: 12/12 source keys match the owner-verified mapping and
12/12 committed review answers match the source keys.

Narrowed policy. ADR-017 is rescoped to a single named route,
deterministic_legacy_admission, establishing recomputed correctness only.
originalGeneration.status stays unverified and independentReviewStatus is
recorded as not_established_unknown_origin.
isProductionGradeIndependentReview is explicitly not modified. All Phase 1
refusals stay active and the PR #74 publishable allow-list is not reopened.

Deferrals. vr-001, vr-016, rc-001, rc-002, rc-003 and the shared reading
passage are DEFERRED with existing reviews preserved as advisory evidence.
Nothing is retired, rewritten or re-authored. No Class A requirement depends
on a provider API review: Google returned 404 then 402 and OpenAI returned
429, so no authenticated external review exists for any provider.

Corrected claims. Re-authoring no longer claimed to eliminate IP risk or to
yield verifiable provenance (live_provider is unimplemented; manual_external
is defined in-repo as untrusted). Originality evidence can now record
matches, uncertainty, inconclusive runs and rejection, and asserts no
zero-risk or copyright position. Approval authentication and the
legacy-origin ledger are stated as separate, unmet security design
requirements. The unevidenced cross-provider "statistically improbable"
claim is withdrawn.

Content preserved. No answer key, stem, option, explanation, passage,
difficulty value or hash is altered. vr-001 and nr-023 remain medium.
Admitting seven items does not authorise releasing a shortened sample.

Verified: reconcile.py deterministic on re-run; 24 doc key/difficulty
assertions cross-checked against the reconciliation; cited code facts
re-read from the branch; validate:questions, questions:validate-ledger and
content:validate-scholarship-drafts all pass.

ADR status remains PROPOSED.

Independent policy review of 63ec92fe returned REQUEST CHANGES. All four
findings are corrected in place, with the withdrawn claim recorded next to
each correction so a re-reviewer can check what was wrong.

P1-1 - threat model T1 credited knownCandidateProvenanceSchema with three
protections it does not have. Verified against candidate-provenance.ts:
candidateGenerationEvent does not exist anywhere in src/; promptVersion is a
nonempty string, not an integer; promptHash is optional and is not validated
as a 64-char hex digest. Also records that contentHash is not hex-validated
and that the known schema is not strict(). States that schema validation
cannot authenticate historical generation, and restates privileged-writer
fabrication plus manifest re-sealing as an OPEN technical trust-boundary
weakness rather than a Zero Fabrication policy violation. Both prerequisites
retained.

P1-2 - T4 credited the first-party recompute with catching the maths-014
ambiguity. It did not: the solver returned an identical clean result before
and after the fix, because option_match_ambiguous detects option collision,
not interpretive ambiguity. Attribution corrected to the external advisory
review; the finding, the corrected closure premise and the later PASS are all
preserved. Adds a mandatory editorial interpretation check (spec 4.2
component 4, ADR requirement 2, schemas 4a) and a prompt-to-solver review of
the five in-scope questions, which flags nr-022 as having the weakest binding
(givens [8]; both ratios hard-coded in the solver). No content altered.

P2-1 - withdraws the claim that with two providers "at most one can share
lineage" so "at least one lineage-independent review always survives". Two
providers are stronger corroboration; they cannot guarantee lineage
independence when the generator is unknown. Class B/C stay deferred.

P2-2 - reconcile.py now models two separately bound review events instead of
one aggregate. Each evidence and packet hash is recomputed from committed
bytes and compared against the committed claim; all four agree.
packet-reviewed-original.json (c82c57d7) is distinguished from the current
packet.json (5bb76447). Adds a preflight vs source-register cross-check:
12/12 agree on raw and publication hashes, and 12/12 on candidate hashes
under documented sidecar semantics.

Verification: 12/12 source keys match; 12/12 review answers agree; zero
inconsistencies; vr-001 and nr-023 remain medium; five-item scope unchanged,
nr-001 conditional, vr-032 deferred; reconciliation byte-identical across
consecutive runs; typecheck and validate:questions pass.

Documentation only. No schema, gate or content change. PR #73 untouched.
ADR-017 remains PROPOSED.

commits.messageBody:
Second independent policy review of eb83708f returned REQUEST CHANGES with
one P1 and three P2 findings. All four are addressed, each recorded beside
the claim it replaces.

P1 - the editorial interpretation check existed only as a standalone schema
and was absent from the assembled bundle and the gate, so the mandatory
requirement was unreachable. schemas.md section 9 now carries a required
editorialInterpretation member with superRefine cross-bindings: candidate id
and revision must equal the binding's, boundContentHash must equal both the
binding and the recompute hash, and the solver identifier and givens shown to
the reviewer must equal those the recompute executed. Records that a bundle
is self-consistent data, so the gate must re-derive solver identity, givens
and content hash from the live registry rather than trust the bundle.
firstPartyRecomputeEvidenceSchema gains solverIdentifier to make that binding
possible; editorialInterpretationCheckSchema gains candidateId,
factoryRevision and reviewerQualification. gate-and-test-changes.md adds
section 3.2.1 as a mandatory staging condition that fails closed even when
numeric recompute passes, plus adversarial cases 18a-18q and the two nr-022
regression cases: case A (word-only mutation against the recorded hash must
fail content_hash_mismatch) and case B (same mutation re-hashed may pass
numeric recompute but must be refused absent genuine editorial evidence for
that revision, with no hard-coded revised key). pr-73-migration-plan.md adds
phase 2e step 2 and section 6.1, revision-bound and sourced from the live
registry. Age-suitability remains separate throughout.

P2-1 - solver-coverage.md implied a content change could leave checked hashes
unchanged. Corrected: prose is inside hashJson(question), so a word-only edit
IS detected against a recorded hash. The real and narrower exposure is fresh
recomputation against newly hashed content, which cannot detect changed
written relationships. Both nr-022 and maths-014 entries rewritten.

P2-2 - the maths-014 ambiguity was surfaced by the manually submitted ChatGPT
advisory review (manual_user_attested, chatgpt-unversioned, no API envelope),
not by a qualified human SME. ADR-017, the specification and threat model T4
corrected; the qualified editorial check is recorded as new, mandatory and
never yet performed for any candidate. REVISE and PASS records preserved.

P2-3 - the README claimed the reconciliation was not regenerated and was
byte-identical to the reviewed versions. True at 63ec92fe, false from
eb83708f. Replaced with an audit history separating unchanged source and
review evidence from regenerated output, which is reproducible but is NOT
byte-identical to what the first review saw.

Verification: all six evidence requirements appear in ADR, specification,
schemas, gate design and migration plan; 12/12 source keys match; 12/12
review answers agree; zero inconsistencies; 12/12 raw, publication and
candidate hashes agree; vr-001 and nr-023 remain medium; scope unchanged at
five with nr-001 conditional and vr-032 deferred; reconciliation regenerates
to the committed bytes; typecheck passes.

Documentation only. reconcile.py and the reconciliation outputs are untouched
this round. No schema, gate or content change. PR #73 untouched at dcb60a80.

commits.messageBody:
CONFIRMED and blocking. schemas.md section 9 required the editorial record's
hash to equal BOTH binding.publicationContentHash AND recompute's bound hash.
Those are different domains, so the pair was unsatisfiable and would have
rejected every genuine bundle for all five in-scope candidates.

Investigation, reproduced with the repository's own hashJson,
candidateQuestionSchema, buildPublishedQuestion and canonicalQuestionHash:

  D1 rawQuestionHash       = hashJson(raw)
  D2 factoryCandidateHash  = hashJson(candidateQuestionSchema.parse(candidate))
  D3 publicationContentHash= canonicalQuestionHash(buildPublishedQuestion(c).question)

D2 is the attestation domain: verifyFirstPartyScholarshipAttestation computes
hashJson(question) and its only production call site passing an expected hash
(publication/eligibility.ts) supplies provenance.contentHash, which the legacy
schema pins to repositoryImport.candidateHash. Running the real attestation
confirms it for all five: expected=D2 returns ok, expected=D3 returns
content_hash_mismatch. D1 and D2 coincide for the five only because none
carries a solver sidecar.

The D2->D3 mapping was verified: canonicalQuestionHash(buildPublishedQuestion(
candidate).question) reproduces the recorded publicationContentHash exactly for
all five. It is therefore derivable, and the gate must derive it rather than
trust it, because legacy-import/bindings.ts currently copies it verbatim from
the source register.

Corrections:
- schemas.md: new section 0 documenting the three domains with verified values;
  component hash fields renamed to be domain-explicit
  (boundFactoryCandidateHash, reviewedFactoryCandidateHash) so cross-domain
  copying is a type-level mistake; new section 4b publication projection
  binding; section 9 superRefine corrected and extended with explicit
  domain-confusion detection; verifier rules now require independent
  recomputation of D1, D2 and D3 and resolution of solver identifier and
  givens from the live registry.
- gate-and-test-changes.md: staging conditions and 3.2.1 corrected to D2; new
  section 4.4a-H with cases 18w-18ae including a uniformly-D3 bundle, a
  derived-D3 check, and a positive control that would have caught this defect.
- spec, ADR-017, pr-73-migration-plan, solver-coverage, threat-model T6:
  domains named explicitly wherever a hash is bound or collected.
- README: H-1 recorded with the before/after domain table.

Verification: all six evidence requirements still present in all five contract
documents; 12/12 source keys match; 12/12 review answers agree; zero
inconsistencies; vr-001 and nr-023 remain medium; scope unchanged at five with
nr-001 conditional and vr-032 deferred; reconciliation regenerates to the
committed bytes; typecheck and validate:questions pass.

Documentation only. No factory code, schema, gate, content, approval or
production data changed. PR #73 untouched at dcb60a80. ADR-017 remains
PROPOSED.

commits.messageBody:
Independent adversarial review of 3b56e157 confirmed the H-1 diagnosis and
fix as correct and independently reproduced, and returned REQUEST CHANGES on
one P1 and four P2. All five addressed; each correction records the claim it
replaces.

R4-P1 - case 18ae, the stated H-1 regression guard, could not detect an H-1
recurrence. It described a bundle "missing editorial evidence" that
nonetheless "passes the hash-domain checks", which is impossible:
editorialInterpretation and publicationProjection are required members, and
Zod runs superRefine only after the base parse succeeds, so refinements (b),
(b2), (f) and (g) would never execute. The test asserted refusal, would have
got refusal for the wrong reason, and would have stayed green if an
unsatisfiable hash condition were reintroduced. Rewritten as case H9:
schema-complete bundle, explicit assertion that safeParse succeeds with zero
issues, gate refusing only on approval and ledger.

R4-P2-A - schemas.md section 0 called eligibility.ts the only production call
site supplying an expected hash; derive-answer.ts:867 also does, passing
hashJson(question) over the object under test. Corrected to "externally
recorded"; the D2 conclusion is unaffected.

R4-P2-B - publicationProjectionBindingSchema.recomputedByVerifier was a
z.literal(true) commented "a bundle author cannot assert it", which is
backwards for a submitted-bundle schema and contradicted Rule 1. Field
removed; recomputation is gate output, not bundle input.

R4-P2-C - "the bundle cannot currently validate into an admissible state" is
not what z.never().optional() does; omission parses. Corrected in schemas.md
section 9 and threat-model T5. This matters because case H9 depends on a
complete bundle parsing cleanly.

R4-P2-D - source-evidence-reconciliation.md claimed "This document is
therefore generated, not written... No value is transcribed by hand." False:
reconcile.py emits only the JSON, and the markdown's tables are hand
transcribed. Corrected in its sections 1 and 8, the README tables, and
threat-model T7, which now carries this as an open instance of threat T7
itself. The transcription was independently verified correct across all 12
rows of both tables.

Also from the same review's non-blocking observations: pinned refinement (d)
to the registry givens array in declared order, closing a latent H-1-shaped
hazard (sameNumbers is order-sensitive, the attestation compares a set);
required the verifier to fail closed on a non-ok buildPublishedQuestion
rather than dereference .question; ADR requirement 2 now names D2; section 4
test cases relabelled C/R/O/I/E/H/N/A/S/G/X, removing two numbering
collisions; spec records that its component numbering differs from the ADR's.

Verification: all six evidence requirements present in all five contract
documents; 12/12 source keys match; 12/12 review answers agree; zero
inconsistencies; vr-001 and nr-023 remain medium; scope unchanged at five
with nr-001 conditional and vr-032 deferred; reconciliation regenerates to
the committed bytes and reconcile.py is untouched; typecheck passes.

Documentation only. PR #73 untouched at dcb60a80. ADR-017 remains PROPOSED.

commits.messageHeadline: docs(governance): correct final-review provenance; add Phase 2b A-0 a…

commits.messageBody:
…t models

Three corrections to the Phase 2b A-0 plan, all from direct verification.

1. The proposed CODEOWNERS assigned `.github/allowed_signers` and
   `.github/CODEOWNERS` to @Vishwas2018 alone. That establishes no independent
   code owner and must not be read as two-party authorisation.

   Verified why: `owner.type` is `User` (personal account, not an
   organisation) and `GET /collaborators` returns exactly one principal,
   @Vishwas2018 with `role_name: admin`. Zero pending invitations, zero teams,
   zero webhooks. A CODEOWNERS rule can only name a principal with write
   access, so every rule this repository can express today resolves to the
   owner.

   Independent signer-registry protection is therefore marked **BLOCKED**, not
   deferred. Administrator bypass is explicitly rejected as a substitute: a
   bypass recorded in a log the bypassing party controls is visible to that
   party, not authorised by a second one. Unblocking is specified as U-1..U-7 —
   a genuinely independent human (not a second account of the owner's, not a
   bot), out-of-band identity verification with 2FA and signing, `write` and
   deliberately not `admin`, independent ownership of the signer registry and
   of CODEOWNERS itself, required approval for protected paths, stale-review
   dismissal plus `require_last_push_approval`, and `enforce_admins`.

   The reviewer's username is a placeholder, `@<independent-reviewer>`; no
   username is invented. Three technical points are recorded: listing two
   owners on a line weakens it to "either may approve", so the two
   self-authorisation paths name the reviewer only; CODEOWNERS must own itself
   or the protecting rule can be deleted first; and a reviewer-authored
   registry change deadlocks, which is fail-closed and must not be "fixed" by
   adding the owner back.

   New section 2.3 addresses administrator control of protection itself
   (G-10). An admin can disable `enforce_admins`, act, and restore it, so it is
   detective, not preventive. Independent control would require migrating to an
   organisation with separated roles and an org-level ruleset excluding repo
   admins from bypass — unavailable on a personal account. External
   auditability is available now via a protection-event webhook to an endpoint
   whose credentials the admin does not hold, or an external polling monitor;
   both are recorded with their limits, including that an admin can delete a
   webhook so silence must also alert. The personal-account security log is
   visible only to the person whose actions it records and is explicitly not
   counted as independent.

2. The instruction to remove `continue-on-error` from `scholarship-drafts` was
   outdated and is removed. Verified against `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on
   current `dev` (identical on this branch): the job at line 87 is a plain
   blocking job, there is no `continue-on-error` at job or step level anywhere
   in the file, and no `if: always()`. `git log -S` shows it was removed in
   `02a0b3ac`. The job ran and passed on both runs of this branch's head.

   Its real gap is that branch protection does not list it as a required
   status check, so a red run is visible but not blocking. That is a
   settings-only fix, and the recommendation to require it on both `dev` and
   `main` is preserved, subject to separate owner authorisation. No workflow
   file is modified.

3. New section 5 distinguishes two approval trust models: (A) GitHub
   pull-request approval protecting code and governance changes, and (B)
   authorised, revision-bound human approval of individual questions —
   requirement 6 and Standing Rule 8 `approvedBy`.

   Six independently sufficient reasons A does not satisfy B: it approves a
   diff not a question-at-revision; write access is not an authorised editorial
   role; it carries no D2/D3 hash binding; it is GitHub-side state the gate
   cannot re-derive; it is mutable by the party it constrains; and its
   independence is blocked here anyway. A is a necessary precondition for B,
   never a substitute.

   Recommended architecture for B, as design guidance only: a detached
   asymmetric signature over a canonical, domain-separated, versioned payload
   binding reviewer identity and authorised role, candidate identity and
   revision, the D2 factory-candidate hash and the D3 publication hash, and an
   explicit closed-enum decision; a committed code-owned key registry with
   roles, validity and revocation, where a writer can never authorise their own
   key; a stated retroactive-versus-prospective revocation policy as an owner
   decision; and verification by re-derivation at admission and again at
   publication, since content can be re-projected in between.

* fix(singapore-maths): stop sample route crashing behind its own flag

With SINGAPORE_MATHS_SAMPLE_ENABLED unset — the state of every Vercel
Preview deployment, since the variable is not configured on the project —
the sample route took its Coming Soon branch and passed the resolved
catalogue entry to <ProgrammeComingSoon>. That entry carries `icon`, a
React component, and the page is a Server Component rendering a Client
Component, so React rejected the function at render time:

  Error: Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components unless
  you explicitly expose it by marking it with "use server".
    {slug: ..., icon: function icon, ...}  digest: '4109859521'

The throw landed in the /practice segment boundary, so both
?year=3 and ?year=5 returned 500 and rendered "We couldn't load the
practice catalogue." before any question was loaded. The catalogue and
the fixtures were never at fault.

Pass `programmeSlug` instead, as the five sibling programme pages already
do; the client resolves the entry itself.

* fix(singapore-maths): gate the sample on deployment AND backend, fail closed

Review correction to the default-on behaviour. Availability by default
outside Vercel production was too broad: it also turned the sample on for
any hosted Preview with no opt-in, and for a local app pointed at the
hosted production Supabase project, which is where a child's practice
submissions would then have been authenticated.

isSingaporeMathsSampleAllowed now answers two questions, and refuses
unless both are explicitly, verifiably true: is this a deployment allowed
to show drafts, and is the backend it would authenticate against a safe
one. The decision, in order:

  1. VERCEL_ENV === "production" is refused first and unconditionally.
  2. SINGAPORE_MATHS_SAMPLE_ENABLED=0/false is an explicit opt-out,
     honoured everywhere.
  3. An unidentifiable Supabase target (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL missing
     or unparseable) is refused: an unknown backend is never a safe one.
  4. The production project is never an accepted target. Declare it as
     PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF and any deployment pointed at it is
     refused, whatever else is set.
  5. Off-Vercel is a convenience mode needing no opt-in, but only against
     an isolated backend (Supabase host 127.0.0.1/localhost/::1). A local
     app on a remote project is refused — this repo's own .env.local
     points at the hosted project.
  6. A hosted Preview requires BOTH an explicit opt-in and a verified
     non-production binding: SINGAPORE_MATHS_SAMPLE_SUPABASE_REF must
     name the project ref the deployment actually uses, with
     PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF declared to check it against. An
     unset variable never enables the sample on Preview.
  7. Any other VERCEL_ENV value fails closed.

The decision is also exported as singaporeMathsSampleAvailability(), which
returns a stable reason code, so a refusal can be explained and asserted
rather than inferred from a bare false.

* fix(landing): visible keyboard focus, solid focus outline, 44px standalone link targets

Phase A of the landing UI/UX audit (D-03, D-05, D-06). No visual redesign.

D-03 focus visibility
- Focus-driven scene scrolling is now instant (scrollTo behavior "instant"),
  for focus only; progress-rail clicks stay smooth. The tested contract
  "tabbing into an off-screen scene brings it on screen" is unchanged.
- The Chapter 2 hand-off CTA ("Explore all programs") now brings its layer
  on screen when focused; it used to take focus at opacity 0 with no ring.
- Shift+Tab from Chapter 2 into the Chapter 1 hero controls (covered by the
  Chapter 2 stage) scrolls back to the Explore hold.
- The fixed mobile CTA bar no longer hides a focused control
  (scroll-padding-bottom while the bar is shown).

D-06 focus ring
- The 30% brand halo measures 1.48:1 on ivory (WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1). Every
  focusable .lp-root control now also gets a solid 2px outline: brand purple
  (about 9:1 on ivory), white on dark surfaces. The halo stays as decoration.
- underlineLinkClasses now carries the halo (links fell back to the browser
  default outline). docs/design.md section 20 amended accordingly.

D-05 link targets
- underlineLinkClasses({ standalone: true }) adds an invisible ::after hit
  area (45px effective height) to the scene CTA links. No margin or padding
  change, so layout and underline position are untouched; inline links are
  not enlarged.

Tests: e2e/landing-keyboard-focus.spec.ts (full forward and reverse Tab walks
at 375/430/768/1024/1440/1920, reduced motion, 200% zoom emulation, ring
contrast, target sizes) and src/tests/unit/landing-focus-scroll.test.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(landing): natural-flow fallback for short desktop viewports; skip-link focus contrast

A pinned stage is one viewport tall with its copy above the progress rail. On short
viewports that does not fit: at 1024x576 the Chapter 2 rail covered the scene CTAs,
and at 1280x633 it covered Chapter 3 "Explore practice" and Chapter 4 "Parent guide"
(WCAG 2.4.11, pre-existing on origin/dev). Chapter 4's cards also ran under the rail
and off the screen up to ~800px.

- Pin only when wide AND tall enough: cinematicMotion.pinnedMinHeight (700) for
  Chapters 1-3 and chapter4.pinnedMinHeight (880). Below it, chapters are natural
  flow like reduced motion. JS (usePinnedViewport) and CSS (`short:` variant, CTA-bar
  scroll padding) read the same number; a unit test ties them together.
- Neutral inline styles in natural flow: framer-motion leaves the last inline opacity
  when `style` is removed, so a resize from pinned to natural flow left Chapter 2
  scenes invisible.
- Skip link focus ring: orange (1.87:1) -> brand purple over a white ring (8.85:1).
- Remove the documented 1024x576 exception; add regression coverage at the owner's
  nine viewports, 1280x633 CTA focus, resize both ways, reduced motion, skip link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(landing): wait for hydration in 1440x900 focus tests; add mixed-layout boundary viewports

The tests waited for `position: sticky`, which server-rendered CSS already
satisfies, so a Tab could land before the Chapter 2 focus handlers were
attached. Wait instead for the scene's inline opacity (the app's own
choreographed-state output), which is committed with the handlers.

Adds the 1280x780 mixed layout and the 879/880/881px Chapter 4 boundary
viewports. Adds a pending (test.fixme) regression test for a reproduced
pre-hydration defect: a scene link focused before hydration is left at
opacity 0 and obscured once the page hydrates. No application change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(landing): recover Chapter 2 focus placed before hydration

Focus that lands on a server-rendered Chapter 2 control before React hydrates
starts a native smooth scroll and fires no focus handler; hydration then fades
that scene to opacity 0 with focus still on it. Once the stage first becomes
choreographed, hold the focused layer's anchor for a bounded number of frames
(max 45), releasing on any wheel/touch/key/pointer input or unmount. Focus is
never moved. Replaces the fixme test with real-Tab scene, hand-off and
no-scroll regression tests.

* fix(landing): keep keyboard focus across the Chapter 3/4 hydration tree swap

Chapters 3 and 4 render a different element tree once they become choreographed
(server render and the first client render are natural flow), so focus placed
before hydration was on a node React then removed: focus fell to <body>, the
browser's smooth scroll ran on to a meaningless offset and the next Tab repeated
the same control. Identical on origin/dev.

A FocusKeeper at the top of each tree records the focused control's tree-independent
key (container + position) in its unmount cleanup, which React runs before the
subtree's nodes are removed, and the replacement tree's keeper restores it on mount
only if focus really fell to <body>: once, without scrolling, then a bounded
(90 frame) anchor hold that any wheel/touch/key/pointer input releases. Each tree's
keeper has a distinct key (otherwise React reuses one instance and nothing unmounts)
and the section ref is read at cleanup time (it is still null at the first mount).
Natural-flow, reduced-motion and short-viewport layouts never swap trees, so the
keeper does nothing there. The cinematic animation system is untouched.

Stacked on #82 (same two chapter files).
